notes:
A site built on a developer's machine updates Kickstarter there first, then
deploys. This release makes the Updates screen and the command line hold to
that, shows when a site's own theme still runs on a build made for an older
Kickstarter, and gives developers one command to bring a site's theme in
line with a new Kickstarter.

### For site administrators
- The Updates screen no longer offers an update on a local or development
  copy of a site, or when the installed Kickstarter is a development copy
  rather than a release build. On a developer's machine those tools are
  what the site's own theme is built with; the screen says to update there
  with wpdev or by hand, then test and deploy.
- On a live or staging site whose Kickstarter is still the development copy
  a migration carried, the screen says to replace it once from the command
  line (or with wpdev deploy). After that, updates work from the screen as
  before.
- When a site has its own child theme, the screen ends with an
  information line: which Kickstarter version the site's theme was built
  against, and that after the update it should be rebuilt and deployed by
  the developers. It never blocks the update.
- Tools > Site Health shows the same: "The child theme was built against
  another Kickstarter version" (recommended) until the site's theme is
  rebuilt for the installed Kickstarter.

### Added
- `npm run parent:adopt` in a site's child
  (`scripts/parent-adopt.mjs --child .`): after a new parent is in place
  beside the child, it checks the parent against its manifest, sets every
  devDependency and script the template's `package.json` lists to the
  template's value (the child's own ones stay), brings in the template's
  files by class (replaced whole, reported for review, missing lines
  appended, or add-only JSON merges of `.wp-env.json` and
  `.claude/settings.json`), then runs `npm install`, `npm run build:prod`,
  `npm run validate-acf` and `npm run parent:verify`. It never touches the
  parent and never runs wp-env. `--dry-run` writes and runs nothing;
  `--json` prints one object. Review items alone exit 0, a failed step
  exits 1, bad usage or a folder that is not a child of this parent exits 2.
  `Requires Kickstarter` is never changed.
- `"kickstarter"` in a child's `package.json`: the parent version it was
  last brought in line with, written by `child:create` and `parent:adopt`,
  which reports it as the version it came from.
- The Updates screen's first preflight row, "The installed parent is a
  production build", and a new access condition, "Not a local or
  development site". A last row, information only, names the version the
  active child's build was made against (`built_against` in its
  `build.json`).
- A Site Health test, `codehills_child_build`: recommended when the active
  child's `built_against` differs from the installed parent, good when they
  are equal, absent without a child or its `build.json`.
- `wp codehills build verify` prints, after its result and without
  changing its exit code, one line per child built against another parent:
  `child <slug> built against <x>, parent is <y>` (a fixed format wpdev
  parses; `docs/commands.md`).
- `docs/local-dev.md`, "Updating the parent": `wpdev update <key>`, or by
  hand (the dev ZIP, `SHA256SUMS`, the old parent moved aside, unpack,
  `npm run parent:adopt`, `npm run env:setup`, commit).
- `npm run test:parent-adopt` (fixture parents and children, npm mocked),
  run in CI.

### Changed
- `wp codehills build install` on a local or development site refuses to
  replace a parent unpacked from the dev ZIP (its manifest, no
  `build.json`) without `--force`. On staging and production it replaces it
  as before and says "Replacing the development copy (the dev ZIP) a
  migration carried with the production build."
- `docs/deploy.md`: route B and "Updating the parent from wp-admin"
  describe the environment rule and the local-first order (update locally,
  test, deploy); a wp-admin update on production leaves the child built
  against the old parent until it is redeployed.
- `ThemeUpdater::environment()` gives the preflight its environment, so the
  tests, whose throwaway key only a local site trusts, run the update as a
  production site. `scripts/skills-sync.mjs` takes the template's skills
  folder as an argument (default unchanged).

### Upgrade notes
- **Existing child sites get `parent:adopt` by running it once from the new
  parent.** After the 2.6.3 dev ZIP is in place beside the child (wpdev
  update, or by hand: `docs/local-dev.md`, "Updating the parent"), run, in
  the child:

  ```bash
  node ../codehills-kickstarter/scripts/parent-adopt.mjs --child .
  ```

  which also adds the `parent:adopt` script to the child's `package.json`.
  From then on it is `npm run parent:adopt`. Its first run reports the
  version it came from as "not recorded": a child made before 2.6.3 has no
  `"kickstarter"` in its `package.json` yet. Review the "Needs review"
  items (the 2.6.3 line in the child's `CLAUDE.md` is one), then
  `npm run env:setup`, restart wp-env, test and commit.
- **A local or development site no longer updates its parent from
  wp-admin**, and `wp codehills build install` there refuses a dev-ZIP
  parent without `--force`. Update it with wpdev or by hand, test, deploy.
- **Route B is unchanged on a server**: the first `build install` after a
  migrator replaces the dev copy it carried without `--force`, and says
  so. A staging or production site whose parent is still that dev copy is
  told on the Updates screen to do that once.
- **wpdev** can parse the new `build verify` line
  (`child <slug> built against <x>, parent is <y>`) and build
  `wpdev update` on `parent:adopt --json`.
